refnamediv.refpurpose: Configure additional binary formats for executables at boot

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: At boot, systemd-binfmt.service8 reads configuration files from the above directories to register in the kernel additional binary formats for executables.

refsect1.title: Configuration Format
refsect1.para: Each file contains a list of binfmt_misc kernel binary format rules. Consult the kernel's Kernel Support for miscellaneous Binary Formats (binfmt_misc) documentation file for more information on registration of additional binary formats and how to write rules.
Empty lines and lines beginning with ; and # are ignored. Note that this means you may not use those symbols as the delimiter in binary format rules.

refsect1.title: BPF Handlers
refsect1.para: Rules of type B are matched and dispatched by a BPF handler, which the rule names in its interpreter field, see bpf-backed handlers. The handler has to be registered before the rule can be. If a file handler.bpf.o exists in one of the directories listed above, the binfmt_misc_ops struct_ops map in this BPF object is registered as the handler right before the rule is written. The object must contain exactly one struct_ops map, and the name the map sets for the handler must match the file name. The rule keeps the handler alive on its own, so nothing else is left registered once the rule is written. If no such file exists, the handler is expected to have been registered by other means already.
Registering a handler from a BPF object requires libbpf and a kernel built with CONFIG_BINFMT_MISC_BPF (Linux 7.3 or newer).

example.title: /etc/binfmt.d/elf-origin.conf example:
example.programlisting: # Let the BPF handler from /usr/lib/binfmt.d/elf_origin.bpf.o pick the loader :elf-origin:B::::elf_origin:
